subject.title: refactor(packages): DM-policy contract suite, dead routes, package folds

question: Should the five existing ACP and memory-host SDK subpaths remain supported compatibility exports, or should maintainers explicitly approve their removal as a public plugin-package contract change?
rationale: The branch establishes that OpenClaw itself can use the canonical owners, but it does not establish that installed external plugins never import these exported subpaths; choosing permanent API removal needs maintainer intent.

options.title: Retain compatibility exports
options.body: Keep the internal caller migration but leave thin deprecated ACP and memory-host re-export modules so installed plugins continue working.

options.title: Approve a breaking removal
options.body: Document the affected subpaths, release timing, and external-plugin migration path, then accept the intentional breaking SDK change.

recommendation.title: Retain compatibility exports
recommendation.body: Keep the internal caller migration but leave thin deprecated ACP and memory-host re-export modules so installed plugins continue working.

likelyOwner.reason: The supplied context shows steipete driving and assigning this cross-package ownership refactor.
